title: Augmented strict adic reduction under ringed open extension
statement:
Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and let $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_W$ be the completed coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $n\ge1$. Identify $A_T|_W=A_W$ and $(P_n)_T|_W=(P_n)_W$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $e_!$ mean sheafification of the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], on modules, complexes and strict towers. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$
$$\rho_{e,K}:(e_!K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}e_!(K_\bullet).$$
For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, it is represented by the actual strict complex map whose $n$-th component is
$$(e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T\longrightarrow e_!\bigl(P\otimes_{A_W}(P_n)_W\bigr),\quad [p]\otimes b\longmapsto[p\otimes b|_W].$$
Brackets denote the extension-presheaf summand indexed by a map to $W$, followed by sheafification. The map is independent of the representative after localization. It commutes with every quotient transition, and with the quotient augmentations $\Delta(e_!P)\to(e_!P\otimes(P_n)_T)_n$ and $e_!\Delta P\to e_!(P\otimes(P_n)_W)_n$, both $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. At level $n$ it also identifies reduction as $(P_n)_T$-modules, before restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $b\ge a\ge1$ it respects the quotient normalization $(K_b\otimes^L_{(P_b)_W}(P_a)_W)\cong K_a$, including the equal-index unit and three-index cocycle of the datum. No completeness of $K$ or quasi-compactness of $e$ is required.

proof.text: Put $R=A_T$, $S_n=(P_n)_T$, and write $J=e_!$. The slice equivalence $W_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq T_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1), and restriction is $F|_W(V)=F(V\to T)$ by its part (3). By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], $(P_n)_T$ is the ring sheafification of the presheaf $C_{n,T}:U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$; since $C_{n,T}(V\to T)$ depends only on the scheme $V$, the restricted presheaf $C_{n,T}|_W$ is $C_{n,W}$ under this equivalence. The natural isomorphism $(C_{n,T}|_W)^\#\cong(C_{n,T}^\#)|_W$ of [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] gives $S_n|_W=(P_n)_W$; its naturality in the presheaf, applied to the postcomposition maps $C_{b,T}\to C_{a,T}$, shows that it carries $q_{b,a}|_W$ to $q_{b,a}$. Restriction is sectionwise and $A_T$ is the sectionwise limit of compatible families, so $R|_W=\varprojlim_n S_n|_W=A_W$ with the same projections. Thus these are the same localized ringed sites with all their ring maps, not discrete constant $A$-coefficient categories. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $J$ is exact. Choose a termwise surjective flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution], $JP\to JC$ is again such a resolution. Applying exact $J$ levelwise is exact on towers, since kernels and cokernels are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; its termwise derived functor is therefore available by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Consequently both sides of the desired comparison can be computed from this single $P$. For the concrete site-equivalence transport used in Lean, first reindex ring and module sheaves sectionwise. This is an algebraic inverse image. Scalar extension along the coefficient-ring isomorphism is the same module transport by [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso]. The ringed-topos K-flat pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] proves that this transport preserves K-flatness and flat terms, so the ringed-slice resolution theorem applies to the actual functor used here.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient-linear ordinary comparison using the normalized scalar-extension/restriction adjunctions of the coefficient datum and the normalized localized extension/restriction adjunction. Transport module sheaves along the concrete slice equivalence and cR,cB. The commuting ring square gives the identity-on-sections natural isomorphism between the two composite right adjoints. Uniqueness of left adjoints therefore gives an isomorphism J_R followed by scalar extension to B, versus scalar extension to C followed by J_B. Independently transpose J_R of the scalar-extension unit through scalar extension on T, using the scalar-restriction comparison. On an extension summand the resulting map sends [x] tensor 1 to [x tensor 1]; B-linearity gives [x] tensor b to [x tensor cB(b)]. The normalized localized adjunction identifies this map with the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism. The two adjunction Hom bijections and generation by extension summands prove uniqueness. Apply its naturality degreewise to obtain actual chain isomorphisms. This supplies the same tensor comparison required by the unit route without invoking a separate projection-formula isomorphism.

proof.text: For any $b\ge a$, the two composites in the transition square for $\delta_P$ send $[p]\otimes r$ to $[p\otimes q_{b,a}(r)|_W]$. Thus the $\delta_{P,n}$ and their inverses form inverse maps of actual strict tower complexes, with the specified quotient transitions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $s\in S_n$ the equality $\delta_{P,n}([p]\otimes rs)=[p\otimes r|_Ws|_W]=s\delta_{P,n}([p]\otimes r)$ proves $S_n$-linearity. Applying extension using $S_n$ as coefficient ring or extending the same sheaf after restriction to $R$ gives the same underlying abelian sheafification; its action is uniquely extended from the same presheaf action [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Hence this is already a comparison of $S_n$-module complexes, and only afterwards of $R$-module complexes by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. In Lean, construct the inverse level maps first. Equality of maps out of the extended restricted tensor follows by the open-extension adjunction and pure-tensor generation. On a generator the transition square is exactly the inverse form of the finite coefficient quotient square. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles these maps; they are objectwise isomorphisms. Inverting gives the prescribed forward level maps and their uniqueness.

proof.text: Termwise extension of the constant tower on $P$ is the constant tower on $JP$, with identity transitions. At every index, $\delta_{P,n}$ sends the quotient augmentation $[p]\mapsto[p]\otimes1$ to $[p\otimes1]$, which is exactly $J$ applied to the augmentation of $P$. The augmentations are strict maps because $q_{b,a}(1)=1$. The equality on extension summands extends uniquely through module sheafification [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], so this is an equality of augmented strict complex diagrams before localization, not just equality of evaluated derived arrows.

proof.text: The quotient normalization is proved on actual complexes, for every P and every degree, without imposing K-flatness: precompose with the inverse balancing isomorphism and use the scalar-extension adjunction to reduce to the generators with scalar 1. Both paths send (([p] tensor r) tensor s) to [p tensor q(r)|W*s|W]. The normalized scalar comparisons and the datum's balancing formula identify these expressions. Equal indices give the tensor unit. For three indices, naturality of the intermediate scalar comparison and the datum's three-index balancing cocycle give the two parenthesizations; applying the same normalized comparison preserves that cocycle. These are actual chain-map equations and remain true after localization. No separate K-flat change-of-rings theorem is needed for these ordinary normalization statements.

proof.text: Naturality of the strict module comparison gives a natural isomorphism on complexes and homotopy categories. Use the generic modelPull_existsUnique argument from [def-sp-constant-reduction-models] with ordinary reduction towers, exact open extension, exact extension on towers and the inverse strict comparison. Package the actual reduction functors, their existing counits, universal properties and computation laws as [def-weil-pbc-derived-reduction-model-data]; this changes none of those objects or maps. The generic helper is instantiated with the actual completed-coefficient module categories. Its resolving class is the flat-term K-flat complexes supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Their localization computes the derived category by [lem-trf-right-fraction-dense-subcategory] and the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The reduction tower counits of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] are invertible on K-flat complexes; Step 1 supplies K-flatness after open extension. The two normalized counit transformations therefore determine a unique descended natural isomorphism. Invert it and compose its equation with the strict chain isomorphism to obtain rho in the stated direction and exactly the required computation equation. This operation also transfers uniqueness. Exactness of extension supplies both endpoint computation isomorphisms. The strict augmentation and normalization equations already proved remain equalities under localization. No completeness or quasi-compactness assumption is used. The two endpoint computations and the strict degreewise comparison specialize generic constructions, definitionally equal to their original formulas; generic ring-sheaf packaging checks category conversions before the completed coefficient limit is substituted.
